translated_text: Bob, I won't be coming to Prague. Not now, and not later. What we feared so much has just happened. I can't anymore! I don't want anything more. This terrible tension has lasted too long. I don't feel strong enough to start a relationship at my age! I'm not complaining. I just have to acknowledge that it can't go on! Unfortunately, we haven't had time to be happy. We've always had so much else to do! We've always preferred to separate and go our separate ways. Coincidence: It started when I was in Pforzheim and traveling. Later came Germany and France. Today it's Prague and London. It's getting harder and harder, more and more unattainable. I wanted to fight against the distance, but I felt like I was fighting alone, and I'm not that strong. I gave up the fight, I felt tired, and alone. You "understood" me, Bob. You've stated time and again that our love is hopeless, and you've never done anything to make it work for you. There was no inner resolve that could have forced you to. So often I tried to explain it to you, while there was still time. You never wanted to understand. – You never considered that a woman needs more than a friend. You always treated me like a good friend. It was nice, Bob; I wanted more. I wanted too much. There will surely be a woman who will give you "that extra something" that I – perhaps – have been waiting for. In London, I had the strong feeling that we had to separate. After your last letter and last card, I no longer have that feeling. – It was naive. Now, Bob? – Can a new, painful togetherness be a new torment? I would have explained to you that everything was hopeless, and you would have agreed with me. I would have left Prague without even uttering a single word. I can't tell you, unfortunately, what you should have done, because I would certainly have had to take your place. If you don't believe you're in love, like me, if you feel that the man, the woman, has come, then the word "want" suddenly disappears. Then you are strong and ready for anything. You no longer feel any effort; then everything can be achieved. But you're not sure if I'm a woman, and from this uncertainty stems the pain of our being together. And because you don't know, I also begin to doubt whether you are THE man of my life. It's a shame that we never got around to traveling to some places together. Time was always so short. We were never together for more than 14 days. It's such a shame, Bob. To be trapped in a vicious cycle. We can't find an end. This is driving me strangely crazy in the long run. Writing this letter is a lot of work for me, do you know anyone? But it's all better this way, my little Bob. I would have loved to have caught up with you one last time. But I couldn't go to Prague to do it. I simply can't! I must be content with holding you in my thoughts one last time, kissing you with love like never before... Bob, I don't think I can manage to keep you as just a good friend. I still love you too much for that. But every now and then I'll write to you. A card to tell you that I'm still alive, that you still live on in me. You, Bob? Never do what you want, what you want. I won't forget you for a long time. Betty.
